defects.rationale: The reset token is built from random.randint(0, 9), a non-cryptographic Mersenne Twister PRNG, making the security-critical token predictable; use secrets instead.

issues.observation: The review reports exactly one finding (insecure_random at line 4). Password-reset snippets of this kind almost always contain additional, independently material defects — e.g. insufficient token entropy/length, missing expiry or single-use invalidation on the stored token, unparameterized SQL or string-formatted queries, token disclosure via logging or the HTTP response, missing user-existence/enumeration handling, and unhandled failure paths. Stopping after the easiest finding leaves interacting defects (predictable token + no expiry + token leak) unreported.

The rationale explains the PRNG weakness generically but does not tie it to the concrete failure path in this snippet (how many digits are concatenated, how the token is then stored/compared, and why an attacker can therefore reconstruct it and take over the account). Without that, the cited line's actual operation is only partially connected to the stated failure.

revision_instructions: Re-read the supplied snippet line by line and add every additional material defect you can support with a specific line: token entropy/length, missing expiry or single-use invalidation, query construction (SQL injection), token exposure in logs or responses, missing error/None handling, and any transaction or commit omission. Keep the total at eight or fewer findings.
Do not modify or remove the existing insecure_random finding at line 4; it is correct. Only strengthen its rationale.

Expand the line 4 rationale to name the concrete attack: state how the token is assembled on that line, the resulting search space, and that an attacker can enumerate or predict it to reset another user's password.

Ensure each new finding cites the exact line containing the responsible operation, uses a taxonomy category, an integer line within the snippet's range, an allowed severity, and a non-empty rationale, with no two findings sharing the same category and line.
